claims.text: The driver cancelled TRP-06052 for rider no-show without ever sending an in-app chat message. The chat log for this trip holds exactly one message and it was sent by the rider (MSG-06052-001, 'Coming down in 3 min', 14:23:40) — the driver sent none, and the trip record's derived contact_before_cancel.message_count for the driver is 0. POL-NS-23 makes a driver-sent in-app message a condition of charging the fee.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is conjunctive: the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before cancelled_at. The two unanswered in-app calls at 14:24:30 and 14:26:50 satisfy only the call limb; because the message limb is unmet the obligation as a whole is unmet — the trip record's own derived contact_before_cancel.obligation_met is false. On the clause's own terms the 5.00 SGD fee must be voided.

Satisfying the free wait does not rescue the fee. On the record the driver marked arrival at 14:22:00 and cancelled at 14:28:05, 365 s later, so the 300 s free wait under POL-NS-21 was running from arrival and had expired (free_wait.cancelled_after_free_wait = true). But POL-NS-22 permits the fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait', and POL-NS-23 layers a further, independent precondition on top: contact by message and call. A satisfied wait is necessary, not sufficient, and the fee stands or falls on POL-NS-23.

Because the contact obligation failed, POL-NS-23 fixes the consequence: the fee is voided and the rider is not charged — FULL_REFUND of the fee charged, with no driver compensation. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the entire contested 5.00 SGD is still outstanding and is what the rider is owed under POL-GEN-03.

The gap is not explained by the rider being uncontactable or absent from the app. The rider's message was read at 14:23:51, before either call was placed, so the driver had the rider's own in-app notice that she was on her way down and had an open chat channel in front of him; he simply never used it. The driver's counterparty statement ('Called 2 times, no pick up') is accurate as to the calls and silent on the message POL-NS-23 requires, so it does not answer the clause.

The GPS trace corroborates the driver's 14:22:00 arrival mark: 25 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage and no gap over 120 s, and the nearest fix to the pickup (index 15 at 14:23:31, accuracy 3 m) lies 3.28 m from the pickup point — well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — while the trace reports zero speed at the pickup from 14:22:01 through to cancellation. POL-NS-21's arrival test is therefore met, and the free wait runs from arrived_at (14:22:00) on this on-demand trip.

The driver honoured the full free wait. POL-NS-21 fixes the free wait at 300 s running from the driver's arrival on an on-demand trip; the wait timer started at 14:22:05, expired at 14:27:05, and the driver did not cancel until 14:28:05 — 365 s after the wait began and 60 s after it expired. The trip record's own free_wait block records cancelled_after_free_wait = true on an artifact that is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

POL-NS-23's call limb is satisfied on the face of the trip record: the complete in_app_calls list shows two calls placed by the driver, at 14:24:30 (rang 22 s) and 14:26:50 (rang 18 s), both unanswered, both before trip_record.cancelled_at at 14:28:05. The driver did not simply cancel on the rider — he tried twice to reach her in-app.

The rider was given every opportunity to board. Her own message — sent 14:23:40 and read 14:23:51 — told the driver she was 'Coming down in 3 min', so she was due at about 14:26:40; the driver called her again at 14:26:50, remained stationary at the pickup (zero speed fixes) and waited until 14:28:05, by which time she had still not appeared. On this record the non-attendance is the rider's, not the driver's failure to wait.

The amount charged is exactly the policy amount: the payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00, fee_matches_policy true and policy_fee_sgd 5.00, and that ledger artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. Where a no-show fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged (5.00 SGD), which under POL-GEN-03 is the money the ruling moves.

The driver concedes the message limb of POL-NS-23 rather than stretch the record. The chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and carries exactly one message — the rider's — with zero messages sent by the driver, and the trip record's contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 and obligation_met = false. On the strict terms of POL-NS-23 that limb fails, and this is the rider's strongest point; the driver does not assert that a chat message was sent when the complete log shows none.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider no refund route on these facts: that clause governs a rider's cancellation following a driver no-show, whereas this trip was cancelled by the driver (cancelled_by DRIVER, reason RIDER_NO_SHOW) only after he had arrived and waited out the free period. Its 5.00 SGD goodwill limb is in any event excluded, because it requires that the driver also failed to attempt contact, and the record shows two attempted in-app calls.

So POL-NS-21's arrival test is met and the 300 s free wait runs from arrival on this on-demand trip. The wait expired at 14:27:05; the driver cancelled at 14:28:05, 365 s after arrival — POL-NS-21 (v2.1 2.2) was therefore satisfied, and I accept the driver's claims on arrival and free wait as fact.

Why the fee still falls. POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3) places a further, independent precondition on the fee: before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before cancelled_at. The two unanswered in-app calls at 14:24:30 and 14:26:50 (EV-TRIP-06052) satisfy only the call limb. The chat log (EV-CHAT-06052, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) contains exactly one message, and it was sent by the rider ('Coming down in 3 min', 14:23:40, read 14:23:51); the driver sent none, and the trip record's own contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 and obligation_met = false. The message limb is unmet, so the obligation as a whole is unmet. The driver's advocate concedes precisely this. The rider's claims on the conjunctive contact obligation and its consequence are accepted; the driver's claim that the rider was given every opportunity, and that POL-NS-24 offers no route, is correct as far as it goes but does not displace POL-NS-23, which the driver's own conduct failed.

Money. The payments ledger (EV-FARE-06052, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 and fee_matches_policy true, with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The refund is therefore the full 5.00 SGD and there is no driver compensation.

The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence, and no party carries a fraud flag.

The trip record's own free_wait block records cancelled_after_free_wait = true on an artifact that is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

POL-NS-23's call limb is satisfied on the face of the trip record: the complete in_app_calls list shows two calls placed by the driver, at 14:24:30 (rang 22 s) and 14:26:50 (rang 18 s), both unanswered, both before trip_record.cancelled_at at 14:28:05. The driver did not simply cancel on the rider — he tried twice to reach her in-app.

The rider was given every opportunity to board. Her own message — sent 14:23:40 and read 14:23:51 — told the driver she was 'Coming down in 3 min', so she was due at about 14:26:40; the driver called her again at 14:26:50, remained stationary at the pickup (zero speed fixes) and waited until 14:28:05, by which time she had still not appeared. On this record the non-attendance is the rider's, not the driver's failure to wait.

The amount charged is exactly the policy amount: the payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00, fee_matches_policy true and policy_fee_sgd 5.00, and that ledger artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. Where a no-show fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged (5.00 SGD), which under POL-GEN-03 is the money the ruling moves.

The driver concedes the message limb of POL-NS-23 rather than stretch the record. The chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and carries exactly one message — the rider's — with zero messages sent by the driver, and the trip record's contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 and obligation_met = false. On the strict terms of POL-NS-23 that limb fails, and this is the rider's strongest point; the driver does not assert that a chat message was sent when the complete log shows none.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider no refund route on these facts: that clause governs a rider's cancellation following a driver no-show, whereas this trip was cancelled by the driver (cancelled_by DRIVER, reason RIDER_NO_SHOW) only after he had arrived and waited out the free period. Its 5.00 SGD goodwill limb is in any event excluded, because it requires that the driver also failed to attempt contact, and the record shows two attempted in-app calls.
